about: Overview

Working with Leaflegal follows four steps. You book a call with our team. We agree your criteria and your price per lead, and show you a sample lead. You sign a partner agreement that sets out how everything works. Then matching enquiries are sent to you as soon as they are checked.

There is no software to install, no platform to learn and no login to remember. Leads arrive in the inbox or CRM your team already uses. When you want to change something, you tell our team and we change it.

Behind those four steps, a lot happens on our side that you never need to see. We run campaigns on social media, search and content aimed at people who need a solicitor now. We ask each person a short set of questions about their matter. We check their mobile number and email address, confirm they want paid help and record their consent to be contacted by a firm. We filter out anyone we cannot help. Only then is an enquiry matched to one firm.

about.h3: The four steps at a glance

list: Book a call. A 30-minute conversation about your practice, your team and what you want.
Agree your criteria and pricing. Practice areas, matter types, locations, monthly volume and your price per lead, with a sample lead to look at.
Sign your partner agreement. Pricing, billing, volumes, delivery and invalid lead rules, all in writing.
Receive leads. Exclusive enquiries by email or CRM, as soon as they are checked.

about: Some things are the same for every partner firm, whatever their size or practice area. Every lead is exclusive to one firm and never resold. Every lead comes with the client's consent record. Every client has been told that Leaflegal is an introduction service, not a law firm, and that we are paid by the firms we introduce. Leaflegal never gives legal advice, and never gives immigration advice in particular.

Almost everything else is your choice. Which practice areas and matter types. Where your clients are. How many leads you want each month. Where leads are delivered. Whether to pause. You can change any of these as your firm changes.

The time from first call to first lead depends mostly on your firm. Some firms know exactly what they want, sign their agreement within days and start receiving leads as soon as matching enquiries come in. Others take longer because a partner or compliance officer wants to review the agreement, or because the firm is setting up a shared inbox and deciding who will call new leads. Neither approach is wrong. It is better to start ready than to start quickly and leave the first leads waiting.
Booking a call
Everything starts with a conversation. You can apply through our partner form, which takes a couple of minutes, and we will arrange a 30-minute call with our team at a time that suits you.

list: The practice areas you handle and the matter types you want most
Matter types you would rather not receive
Where your clients usually are, and whether you work remotely
How you are regulated, and your registration details
Who will call new leads, and how quickly they can usually do it
How many new enquiries your team could take on each month
How you would like leads delivered

about: Ask anything. Firms usually want to know where our leads come from, what the consent wording says, how we decide which firm receives a lead, how pricing works and what happens if a lead has wrong details. We will answer plainly. If we do not think the service is a good fit for your firm, we will say so.

On the call we show you a sample lead in the format you would receive it. You can see every field, how the client's description reads, what the consent record looks like and how it all appears on a phone screen. Many firms find this the most useful part of the conversation, because it shows exactly what their intake team would be working with.
The call does not commit you to anything. It is a chance for both sides to understand whether working together makes sense.

Within a short time of the call, we send your proposal. It sets out the criteria we discussed, your price per lead for each practice area and our honest view of likely volumes. If something in it does not match what you expected, tell us. It is common for firms to adjust a matter type or a location at this stage before moving on to the agreement.
Criteria and price
After the call, we set up your matching criteria and put together a proposal. Your criteria decide which enquiries reach you. Your price per lead depends on those criteria.

Criteria are written in plain words rather than codes, so you can read them and know exactly what you will receive. If you are not sure whether a particular kind of matter would be included, ask us before you sign.
Choose from conveyancing, family law, immigration, debt recovery for businesses, motoring offences, licensing and lease extensions. You can take one area or several, and each is set up separately.

Within each area, choose the matters you want. A family firm might take contested finances and children work but not uncontested divorce. A conveyancing team might take purchases and sales but not remortgages. A commercial firm might take debt recovery above a rough amount owed.

Tell us the towns, counties or regions you cover, or that you work nationally. Matters in six of our areas are in England and Wales. Trademark and immigration enquiries can come from anywhere in the UK.
The minimum is 10 leads a month. Above that you set a monthly cap based on how many enquiries your team can call back quickly.

Your proposal sets out your criteria, your price per lead for each practice area and any other costs, so you can see exactly what you would be agreeing to. We will also give you an honest view of likely volumes. If your criteria are narrow, we will tell you and suggest options.

Imagine a firm with offices in two neighbouring towns. It might choose family law, taking contested finances and child arrangements but not simple divorce, plus conveyancing purchases and sales but not remortgages. It might cover its two towns and the surrounding county for family work, and only its two towns for conveyancing. It might set a monthly cap that reflects how many enquiries its two teams can call back quickly between them. Each area would have its own price. This is only an illustration, but it shows how much of the arrangement is in your hands.
Your agreement
Before your first lead, you sign a partner agreement. It sets out how the arrangement works in writing, so that your firm and Leaflegal both know where they stand.

list: Your price per lead for each practice area
How and when you are billed
Your monthly volume and how to change it or pause
What counts as an invalid lead, the review period for raising one and how it is dealt with

about: Lead buying goes wrong when expectations are unclear. A firm thinks it will receive one thing and gets another, or a disagreement about a lead turns into a dispute about money. Writing everything down at the start avoids that. Your team knows what to expect and what to report, and so do we.

about.h3: Taking a look before you sign

about: Take the time you need to read it. Many firms ask their compliance officer or practice manager to look at it too, especially the sections about referral disclosure and data. If something is unclear, ask us and we will explain.

Your agreement sits alongside your own regulatory duties. You remain responsible for being authorised for the work you take on, for telling clients about the referral arrangement as the SRA Code of Conduct requires, for conflict checks and for handling client data under UK data protection law.

Your agreement records the arrangement as it stands when you sign. Criteria, caps and delivery details often change afterwards as your firm learns what works. Day to day changes such as a new matter type, a different cap or a new delivery address are made by telling our team. Bigger changes, such as a new price for a new practice area, are confirmed with you in writing so the record stays accurate.
Receiving leads
Once your agreement is in place, matching enquiries are sent to you as soon as they have been checked. There is no batching and no waiting for a daily file.
Each lead goes to your firm alone. It is never sent to another firm at the same time and never resold later, so the client is expecting one call, from you.

Leads can be sent by email to one or more addresses, to a shared intake inbox, or into your CRM or case management system using a lead email address or a webhook. Each lead is formatted to be easy to read on a phone.

The client's name, verified UK mobile number and email address. The practice area and matter type. A description in their own words. How urgent it is and any deadline or hearing date. Their location. Confirmation they want paid help. The best time to call, the source, a timestamp and the consent wording they agreed to.

Call as soon as you can. Open with the matter and any deadline. Explain that they made an enquiry through Leaflegal and asked to speak to a solicitor. Be clear about your fees and agree a next step. If they do not answer, leave a voicemail and send an email and a text, then try again.
If a lead has wrong contact details or falls outside your criteria, tell us within the review period in your agreement. If you cannot act because of a conflict, let us know too.

The first few leads are a good chance to test your intake routine. Check that leads are landing where you expect, that notifications are reaching the right people and that whoever calls them knows how to explain the introduction. If anything does not work as planned, such as leads going to the wrong inbox, tell us and we will change the delivery. Small fixes in the first week save a lot of missed calls later.
After launch
Getting started is only the beginning. The firms that do best keep talking to us as they learn what works.
Tell us which leads turned into instructions and which did not, and why if you know. We use that to adjust your criteria and to improve the campaigns that produce enquiries for firms like yours.

Most firms change something in the first few months. They add a matter type that is working well, drop one that is not, widen their locations or raise their cap. Tell our team what you want to change and we will update your matching.
If your team is at capacity, a fee earner is away or you are moving offices, ask us to pause. You receive no leads while paused. When you are ready, we start matching to you again on the same terms.

When someone new joins your intake team, show them a recent lead and walk them through the first call. Make sure they know to mention the Leaflegal enquiry, to explain the referral arrangement in the way your firm does and to record the outcome. A short, shared note on how your firm handles leads keeps the approach consistent as your team changes.
Keep a simple record of each lead and its outcome. Looking at it by practice area once a month shows you where your leads work best and helps you decide where to grow.
Leaflegal does not charge clients anything, and tells every client that it is paid by the firms it introduces. If you are ready to begin, apply to become a partner firm.
faqs: The first call
How do I book a call?

Complete our partner application, which takes a couple of minutes. It asks about your practice areas, how you are regulated, the areas you cover and how many leads you want. We then arrange a 30-minute call with our team at a time that suits you. There is no obligation at this stage.
Who should join the call from our side?

Whoever makes decisions about new business and whoever will handle the leads day to day. In a small firm that may be one person. In a larger firm it is often a partner and a practice or intake manager. Your compliance officer is welcome to join or to ask questions afterwards.
What should I have ready for the call?

A clear idea of the practice areas and matter types you want, the locations you cover, how you are regulated and roughly how many new enquiries your team could call back each month. It also helps to know how you would like leads delivered, such as to a shared inbox or into your CRM.
Will I see a real lead before I commit?

Yes. We show you a sample lead on the call so you can see every field, the client's description, the consent record and how it looks on a phone. You can decide whether it suits your intake team before you agree anything. Many firms find this the most useful part of the call, because it shows the information they will have in front of them before they dial.
Does the call commit me to anything?

No. The call is a chance to understand each other. Nothing is agreed until you have seen your proposal and signed your partner agreement. If we do not think the service is a good fit for your firm, we will tell you. We would rather be honest early than take on a firm the service will not suit.
Can I ask about compliance on the call?

Yes, and many firms do. We can explain our consent wording, how we tell clients about the referral arrangement, which areas we do not cover and how data is handled. Leaflegal cannot give your firm regulatory advice, but we can explain exactly how the service works so your compliance officer can take a view.
Setting up
How are my criteria set up?

We set them up for you after the call, based on the practice areas, matter types, locations and volume you choose. There is no form to fill in on a platform and no settings to manage yourself. If you want to change anything later, you tell our team. Your criteria are written in plain words.
Can I choose more than one practice area?

Yes. Each area is set up separately, with its own matter types, locations and price. Many firms take two or three areas, often with leads for each going to a different team. You can start with one area and add others later, once you have seen how leads fit with your intake. Each area has its own price, set out in your proposal and partner agreement.
Can I exclude certain matter types?

Yes. Within each area, tell us what you want and what you do not. We only send enquiries that fit what you have chosen. You can change your choices at any time. Being specific is better than receiving enquiries you will not act on. If you are unsure whether a kind of matter would be included, ask before you sign and we will explain.
How is my price worked out?

It depends on the practice areas, matter types and locations you choose and the volume you want. We explain how each choice affects the price on the call, then set out your price per lead in your proposal. We do not publish prices because they vary widely. There is no auction, so your price does not move with other firms' bids.
How long does setup take?

Once your criteria, price and delivery are agreed and your partner agreement is signed, leads start as matching enquiries come in. How quickly the first one arrives depends on your criteria. Wider coverage usually produces matches sooner. The main thing that affects timing on your side is how quickly you review the proposal and agreement and set up a place for leads to land. It is better to start ready than to start quickly.
Do I need to change our systems?

No. Leads can arrive by email, which works with any intake process. If your CRM or case management system accepts leads by email or webhook, we can send them straight into it instead. Many firms start with email and move leads into their CRM later. Either way, there is no software to install and no login to manage.
Your agreement
What is in the partner agreement?

It covers your price per lead, billing, volumes, delivery and how invalid leads are handled, including the review period for raising a problem. It is written so your firm knows exactly how the arrangement works before your first lead. Day to day changes such as a new cap or delivery address are made by telling our team, and bigger changes are confirmed with you in writing.
Can I take time to review it?

Yes. Take the time you need. Many firms ask their compliance officer or practice manager to look at it. If anything is unclear, ask us and we will explain. Leads only start once it is signed. There is no pressure to sign quickly. It is better that your firm understands and is comfortable with every part of the arrangement before your first lead arrives.
Does the agreement cover referral disclosure?

Your agreement sets out how the arrangement works. Your duty to tell clients about the referral arrangement comes from the SRA Code of Conduct or your own regulator's rules. Our consent wording tells every client that Leaflegal is paid by the firms it introduces, and we send it with each lead.
How do I end the arrangement?

The terms for ending the arrangement are set out in your partner agreement, which you see and agree before you start. You can also pause at any time if you simply need a break from receiving leads. If you are thinking of stopping because results are disappointing, talk to us first. A change of matter types, locations or intake routine often makes a real difference.
Is the agreement a long term contract?

The length and any notice terms are set out in your partner agreement, which you see before you commit. Leaflegal does not rely on long contracts to keep firms. We would rather you stayed because the leads are worth it to your firm. You can also pause at any time without ending the arrangement.
Do I sign anything before the call?

No. The partner application only asks for basic information about your firm so we can prepare for the call. Nothing is signed until you have seen your proposal and are happy with your partner agreement. The call itself is free of any commitment. Nothing is signed early. Ask us anything first.
Day to day
How quickly will leads arrive?

As soon as each enquiry has been checked. There is no batching or delay. That means you can call while the client is still focused on their matter and expecting to hear from a solicitor. Make sure notifications are switched on for whoever handles new leads, so a lead does not sit unnoticed in a busy inbox.
What should we do when a lead arrives?

Call as soon as you can. Use what the client told us, such as the matter type and any deadline. Explain that they enquired through Leaflegal and asked to speak to a solicitor. Be clear about fees and agree a next step, then confirm it by email. Then record the outcome.
What if leads arrive at night or at weekends?

They wait in your inbox or CRM until someone picks them up. Many firms check first thing each morning and call overnight leads before the day gets busy. Some cover evenings for urgent areas such as motoring and immigration. A short text or email to acknowledge the enquiry and promise a call at a set time can stop the client looking elsewhere in the meantime.
Can leads go to different people?

Yes. We can send leads for different practice areas or locations to different email addresses, to a shared intake inbox, or into your CRM where you can assign them. If you route leads to named people, make sure someone else can see them during holidays and sickness. Many firms find one shared route, with internal assignment, is the simplest way to make sure nothing is missed.
Who do I contact if there is a problem?

Our team. There is no help desk ticketing system or portal. Contact us about an invalid lead, a change of criteria, a pause or anything else, and we will deal with it directly. Because there is no portal, queries are handled by people who know your account. Tell us as soon as you notice a problem so we can put it right before it affects more leads.
Do clients know my firm will call them?

They know that a firm will call them. Every client ticks a box agreeing that their details can be shared with a firm we match them with, and that the firm can contact them by phone, email or text about their matter. When you call, introduce your firm and mention their Leaflegal enquiry.
Do we pay Leaflegal anything when a client instructs us?

Your payments to Leaflegal are for leads, at the price agreed in your partner agreement. How and when you are billed is set out there. Clients do not pay Leaflegal anything, and they agree fees directly with your firm. Your price per lead does not depend on whether the client instructs you or on the fees you earn from the matter. We take no share of your fees.
Changes later
Can I change my criteria after I start?

Yes. Add or remove practice areas or matter types, widen or narrow your locations and raise or lower your cap whenever your firm's needs change. Tell our team and we will update your matching. Most firms adjust something in their first few months, once they can see which matter types and locations bring in the work they want most.
Can I pause leads?

Yes. If your team is at capacity or someone is away, ask us to pause. You receive no leads while paused, and your criteria and price stay the same for when you return. Pausing is useful when a fee earner is on leave, your team is busy with existing work or your office is closing for a holiday. Just tell our team when you are ready to start again.
Will you tell me how my leads are performing?

You see the outcomes better than we do, because you know which clients instructed. Share them with us and we will use them to refine your criteria. We are happy to talk through what we see working for firms in general, without sharing any other firm's details. There is no report to log into.
Can I add a new office or location later?

Yes. Tell us the new towns, counties or regions you want to cover and we will add them to your matching. If the change affects your price, for example because it widens or narrows your coverage a great deal, we will explain that before making it. Leads for a new office can also be routed to its own address or team.
What if our regulation details change?

Let us know straight away. We only match enquiries in areas where you are authorised to act, so changes to your regulator, registration or the work you are allowed to do may change what you can receive. For immigration, this includes any change to an adviser's Immigration Advice Authority level.
